high.title: Vietcap Securities Forecasts VN-Index Could Touch 1,885 Points as Early as August
high.summary:
Following a sharp correction of over 10% during the first three weeks of July, the VN-Index staged a recovery of nearly 4% in the latter half of the month, supported by bottom-fishing demand. The buying momentum emerged as the VN-Index's trailing P/E ratio — excluding Vingroup stocks — fell below two standard deviations from its 10-year median, a valuation level previously seen only during the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020 and the corporate bond crisis in late 2022. From a technical standpoint, Vietcap identifies a strong recovery leg after the index successfully established a base at the 1,665-point support zone. In early August sessions, the index has reclaimed the 200-day moving average and is now approaching the 50-day moving average near the 1,800-point level. Vietcap's base case assigns a 65% probability that the VN-Index will reach 1,885 points within August. **For international fund managers, this signals a potential mean-reversion trade opportunity. The extreme valuation compression warrants close monitoring of foreign flow reversal and macro catalysts that could drive sustained re-rating.**

---

high.title: Bank Deposit Rates as of August 6: ACB Leads Market at 7.8%/Year for 12-Month Term
high.summary:
Vietnam's deposit rate landscape continues to show a pronounced bifurcation between private and state-owned banks. ACB remains the market leader at **7.8%/year** for the 12-month tenor, with LPBank second at 7.3%, Saigonbank at 7.2%, and Bac A Bank at 7.1%. A total of **8 banks now offer 7% or above** for 12-month deposits. By contrast, the Big Four state-owned banks (Agribank, BIDV, Vietcombank, VietinBank) hold steady at **6.8%/year** for 12–18 month tenors and 6.6% for 6–9 month tenors. This widening spread between private and SOE bank rates signals ongoing competition for retail deposits, driven by robust credit growth outpacing deposit mobilization. For bond market participants, elevated deposit rates at private banks create upward pressure on short-to-medium government bond yields, as investors demand comparable returns. The persistence of rates near 7.8% at the upper end also raises questions about whether SBV will need to intervene to prevent deposit cost inflation from feeding through to lending rates and ultimately broader credit conditions. Watch for any SBV guidance on deposit rate caps.

---

high.title: Big Money Unexpectedly Returns: Foreign Investors Net Buy VND 2,200 Billion in Vietnamese Equities in Just 5 Sessions
high.summary:
Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) made a notable reversal during the trading week of August 3–7, 2026, swinging to net buyers of Vietnamese equities after a prolonged period of selling pressure. Over the five-session week, foreigners net bought VND 2,166 billion (~USD 85–87 million) across all exchanges. The bulk of activity was concentrated on HoSE, where net purchases reached VND 2,266 billion, while foreigners were modest net sellers on HNX (VND -88 billion) and UPCoM (VND -12 billion). Top net buy targets included FPT (VND 667 billion) and VIC (VND 617 billion).

The VN-Index gained 32.28 points (+1.86%) on the week, closing at 1,768.06 — consolidating above the key 1,760 level — supported by broad-based recoveries in banking, securities, and real estate sectors. However, profit-taking in the final two sessions caused foreign investors to briefly return to net selling, suggesting conviction may be fragile.

medium.title: Difficult Equity Market Conditions: New Account Openings Drop Sharply
medium.summary: Data from the Vietnam Securities Depository (VSD) shows that approximately 227,000 new domestic investor accounts were opened in July 2026 — a sharp decline from the prior month and the second-lowest monthly figure in the past year. The broader context is significant: the VN-Index fell nearly 7% in July, at one point dipping close to the 1,650-point level, as domestic liquidity stalled and foreign investors aggressively sold, offloading a net VND 11,600 billion (~USD 450 million equivalent) on the Ho Chi Minh Stock Exchange during the month. Cumulative year-to-date account openings now stand at approximately 1.8 million, bringing total individual investor accounts to nearly 13.6 million, equivalent to roughly 13% of the population. **The combination of sustained foreign net selling and weakening retail participation is a key bearish signal for near-term market breadth and liquidity, with direct implications for VND capital account dynamics and equity risk premium.**

medium.title: 56 Securities Removed from Margin-Eligible List by HOSE in August
medium.summary: The Ho Chi Minh Stock Exchange (HOSE) has announced its updated list of securities ineligible for margin trading, with 56 tickers currently restricted as of August 5, 2026. Notable names on the restricted list include APG, APH, DQC, DGC, HVN, LDG, OGC, and others, primarily due to trading suspension, warning, or control status. A separate cohort — including AAN, BVB, GEL, HPA, MZG, and VBB — was restricted due to listing tenure of under six months. Some stocks were removed from the restricted list after rectifying qualifying conditions, including GHC (Gia Lai Hydropower) and TIX, which regained margin eligibility from August 3. **This regulatory update is relevant for leveraged positioning strategies on Vietnamese equities; the contraction in margin-eligible securities may constrain retail leverage capacity and exert additional pressure on liquidity during the current market recovery phase.**

medium.title: Gold Price Surpasses $4,300/oz, Experts Forecast New All-Time Highs
medium.summary:
Gold spot prices broke through $4,300/oz during the Asia morning session on August 6, reaching their highest level since June 18, before pulling back slightly to $4,278/oz by mid-afternoon Vietnam time — still approximately $31/oz above the prior session close. Since July 31, gold has rallied more than 5.8%. Guoxin Futures' chief analyst Gu Fengda attributes the sharp near-term move primarily to a rapid decline in market expectations for further Fed rate hikes, driven by cooling U.S. labor market signals. Concurrently, the USD index and U.S. Treasury yields have fallen sharply, providing additional tailwinds for gold. **Relevance for VND traders:** A sustained USD weakening environment, if confirmed by incoming Fed signals, would reduce depreciation pressure on the VND and could prompt the SBV to ease its defensive FX posture. Lower U.S. Treasury yields also improve the relative attractiveness of emerging market local-currency bonds, including Vietnamese government bonds. Fund managers should monitor whether this gold/USD move reflects a broader shift in global risk appetite that could support VND stability and foreign inflows into Vietnamese fixed income.

---

medium.title: Bank Deposit Rates as of August 4: Rate Structure Unchanged, Private Banks Maintain Elevated Yields
medium.summary: The August 4 deposit rate survey confirms the same rate structure as the August 6 update, with ACB holding at 7.8%/year for 12 months and LPBank having raised its rate to 7.3% at the start of August. The Big Four SOE banks remain anchored at 6.8% for 12–18 month tenors. The data point confirms that the rate increases observed at LPBank are a deliberate adjustment rather than a one-off, and that the competitive pressure on deposit mobilization is structural rather than transitory. For fixed income investors, this sustained elevation in market deposit rates continues to create a challenging environment for government bond demand at current yield levels, and may necessitate a yield adjustment in the primary market.

medium.title: MB Bank Investor Meeting: Confident on 2026 Profit Target, Caps Real Estate Loan Exposure at 13% ±2%
HOSE Updates Margin Restriction List, Including High-Profile Stocks HVN, DGC, DMX...
medium.summary: The Ho Chi Minh Stock Exchange (HOSE) has updated its list of securities ineligible for margin trading, now totaling 57 tickers as of August 7, 2026. Notable restricted names include Vietnam Airlines (HVN), DGC, VMD, DRH, DLG, LDG, OGC, TDH, and TTF. Newly listed DMX (Dien May Xanh Investment JSC, debuted August 6) is restricted due to its sub-6-month listing tenure. Restrictions stem from varied causes: some stocks are under exchange control or trading restriction status (HVN, DGC, DRH, VMD), others are on warning status, and several were excluded due to negative post-tax profits in 2025 or tax law violations. For equity investors, the expanding margin restriction list signals continued regulatory tightening on lower-quality or distressed names, which could compress liquidity and amplify volatility in affected securities. Investors should monitor whether major index constituents face further restrictions.

medium.title: Vietnam's Big4 State Banks See Headcount Fall by 1,100 in H1 2026 as Labour Costs Rise
medium.summary: Vietnam's four largest state-owned commercial banks — Agribank, BIDV, Vietcombank, and VietinBank — collectively shed 1,133 employees in the first half of 2026, bringing total combined headcount to 110,668 as of 30 June 2026, down from 111,801 at end-2025. BIDV recorded the steepest proportional decline (-469 staff, -1.8%), followed by Agribank (-316 staff), which nonetheless remains the largest employer among the group with over 40,263 employees (36%+ of Big4 total). Notably, despite the headcount reduction, labour costs continued to rise across all four institutions, reflecting higher per-employee compensation as banks accelerate digital transformation and process automation. For fixed-income and equity investors, this trend signals continued cost rationalisation at systemically important banks, which should support return-on-equity improvement over the medium term. Tighter staffing at Big4 lenders is also consistent with ongoing operational efficiency drives that could gradually reduce operating cost ratios — a positive structural signal for Vietnamese bank equities. Watch for whether cost savings translate into wider net interest margins or are passed through via more competitive deposit/lending rate offerings.

medium.title: An Important Factor Is Returning to the Stock Market — State Divestment and Equitisation Revival
medium.summary: According to BIDV Securities (BSC), equitisation, state divestment, and share auction activity are showing renewed momentum after years of near-dormancy, with positive signals emerging since 2025 in line with government directives to improve state-owned enterprise (SOE) efficiency. Historically, SOE equitisation waves in 2006–2008 and 2014–2018 were major drivers of equity supply on HOSE and HNX, bringing large-cap names to market and generating transactions worth tens to hundreds of trillions of VND. After 2018, activity stalled sharply. The current revival is relevant to VN-Index watchers as a renewed pipeline of SOE IPOs and block sales could significantly increase free float and tradable supply on Vietnamese exchanges — a key structural catalyst for market upgrade considerations. For international fund managers, this also signals potential capital flow opportunities as large state assets are repriced through public markets. Key risk: execution pace and pricing discipline remain uncertain; previous waves saw significant valuation disputes and delays.

medium.title: Bao Viet Group Deposits Nearly VND 167,000 Billion at Banks, Earning Up to 8.9%/Year Interest Rate, Collecting Nearly VND 5,000 Billion in Interest Income
medium.summary:
Bao Viet Group (HoSE: BVH), Vietnam's largest insurance conglomerate, disclosed its Q2/2026 consolidated financial results, revealing that bank deposits of nearly VND 167,000 billion — representing more than half of its total assets — are earning interest rates of up to 8.9% per annum. Deposit interest income reached VND 4,926 billion in H1/2026, surging 42.3% year-on-year and accounting for approximately 58% of total financial revenues. Bond, bill, and promissory note income contributed an additional VND 2,868 billion (+17.8% YoY). Overall pre-tax profit for H1/2026 stood at VND 2,289 billion, up ~34% YoY, driven primarily by financial investment activities rather than core insurance operations.

**Relevance for traders:** The 8.9%/year deposit rate being offered to a major institutional client signals that Vietnamese bank deposit rates remain elevated at the longer end of the curve. This is a meaningful data point for VND interest rate expectations and bond market positioning — if large institutional depositors can lock in near 9% on bank deposits, demand for government bonds at lower yields faces headwinds. It also suggests banks continue to compete aggressively for stable, long-duration funding, which could support VND liquidity but warrants monitoring for any SBV response.
